title: Too Few: the Spindle and a Virus

scenes.tts: Why would a protein of the cell's spindle shrink the brain more than other organs?
scenes.visual: Title card: Too Few: the Spindle and a Virus. A dividing cell with its spindle and two poles highlighted.
scenes.narration: Why would a protein of the cell's spindle shrink the brain more than other organs?

scenes.tts: Primary microcephaly is recessive. The brain is small, and its layers are usually broadly in order.
scenes.visual: A small cortex with orderly bands beside a normal one. Label: primary microcephaly, recessive.
scenes.narration: Primary microcephaly is recessive. The brain is small, and its layers are usually broadly in order.

scenes.tts: Most of its genes, such as A S P M, make proteins of the spindle pole.
scenes.caption: Most of its genes, such as ASPM, make proteins of the spindle pole.
scenes.visual: The spindle with ASPM, CDK5RAP2 and WDR62 tags at the poles. Label: centrosome, the main microtubule-organizing center.
scenes.narration: Most of its genes, such as ASPM, make proteins of the spindle pole.

scenes.tts: Radial glial progenitors are tall and thin, with a small patch facing the ventricle.
scenes.visual: A tall, thin radial glial cell; a small apical patch at the ventricle is highlighted.
scenes.narration: Radial glial progenitors are tall and thin, with a small patch facing the ventricle.

scenes.tts: In early divisions, the cleavage plane affects how that patch is shared.
scenes.visual: A vertical cleavage plane splits the patch; both daughters keep a piece.
scenes.narration: In early divisions, the cleavage plane affects how that patch is shared.

scenes.tts: Tilt the spindle, and one daughter can get it all. That can change what the daughters become.
scenes.visual: A tilted cleavage plane gives most or all of the patch to one daughter. The daughters' outcomes are shown with question marks, as possibilities, not a fixed fate.
scenes.narration: Tilt the spindle, and one daughter can get it all. That can change what the daughters become.

scenes.tts: But a daughter without the patch can still divide, as a progenitor away from the ventricle.
scenes.visual: The daughter without the patch moves up from the ventricle and divides again. Label: the patch alone does not decide fate.
scenes.narration: But a daughter without the patch can still divide, as a progenitor away from the ventricle.

scenes.tts: In mouse embryos, knocking down A S P M tilted the division plane, and shifted divisions away from making progenitors.
scenes.caption: In mouse embryos, knocking down Aspm tilted the division plane, and shifted divisions away from making progenitors.
scenes.visual: Credit: Fish and colleagues, 2006, mouse embryos. Tilted division planes; fewer symmetric, progenitor-making divisions.
scenes.narration: In mouse embryos, knocking down Aspm tilted the division plane, and shifted divisions away from making progenitors.

scenes.tts: In mouse progenitors, delayed mitosis can also trigger a death that depends on p fifty-three, a sensor of cell stress.
scenes.caption: In mouse progenitors, delayed mitosis can also trigger a death that depends on p53, a sensor of cell stress.
scenes.visual: A progenitor stuck in mitosis fades out. Label: delayed mitosis, p53-dependent death.
scenes.narration: In mouse progenitors, delayed mitosis can also trigger a death that depends on p53, a sensor of cell stress.

scenes.tts: And if a fault recurs round after round, it compounds.
scenes.visual: The doubling tree from chapter 1, with the shrinking bar.
scenes.narration: And if a fault recurs round after round, it compounds.

scenes.tts: Predict. A child with no working A S P M has a markedly small brain, but mice lacking the gene have only a mild reduction. Ferrets have a folded cortex, rich in outer radial glia. Those are progenitors that have left the ventricle but keep dividing. Knock the gene out in a ferret. Less shrinkage, the same, or more?
scenes.visual: A mouse cortex and a ferret cortex side by side. Label: ferret cortex, folded, rich in outer radial glia (progenitors that divide away from the ventricle). Question card: less, the same, or more?
scenes.narration: Predict. A child with no working ASPM has a markedly small brain, but mice lacking the gene have only a mild reduction. Ferrets have a folded cortex, rich in outer radial glia. Those are progenitors that have left the ventricle but keep dividing. Knock the gene out in a ferret. Less shrinkage, the same, or more?
scenes.caption: Predict. A child with no working ASPM has a markedly small brain, but mice lacking the gene have only a mild reduction. Ferrets have a folded cortex, rich in outer radial glia. Those are progenitors that have left the ventricle but keep dividing. Knock the gene out in a ferret. Less shrinkage, the same, or more?

scenes.tts: Much more. The authors traced it to radial glia leaving the ventricle too early. A second reading, still a hypothesis, is that more rounds mean more compounding.
scenes.visual: The ferret cortex shrinks far more than the mouse's. Credit: Johnson and colleagues, 2018: ventricular radial glia displaced too early. Separate panel, labelled illustrative model, not measured in mice or ferrets: with a one-in-ten chance per division of coming out neurogenic for that round, the expected pool is about 77 percent of normal after 5 rounds, 60 percent after 10, 46 percent after 15.
scenes.narration: Much more. The authors traced it to radial glia leaving the ventricle too early. A second reading, still a hypothesis, is that more rounds mean more compounding.

scenes.tts: Now Zika. How do you show a virus causes a birth defect, without testing it in pregnant women?
scenes.visual: A Zika particle. A three-column evidence board appears, empty: epidemiology, pathology, laboratory.
scenes.narration: Now Zika. How do you show a virus causes a birth defect, without testing it in pregnant women?

scenes.tts: Epidemiology. Microcephaly rose after the virus, in time and place. That shows association, not cause or mechanism.
scenes.visual: Column 1 fills: Brazil, 2015, and a look back at French Polynesia. Shows: association in time and place. Cannot show: cause on its own, or mechanism.
scenes.narration: Epidemiology. Microcephaly rose after the virus, in time and place. That shows association, not cause or mechanism.

scenes.tts: Pathology. Virus was found inside a damaged fetal brain. On its own, that cannot show the virus did the damage.
scenes.visual: Column 2 fills: Mlakar and colleagues, 2016. Shows: virus inside a damaged fetal brain. Cannot show, on its own: that it did the damage, or how often.
scenes.narration: Pathology. Virus was found inside a damaged fetal brain. On its own, that cannot show the virus did the damage.

scenes.tts: The laboratory. The virus infected human cortical progenitors most readily, killing some and slowing the rest. A dish cannot show the risk in a pregnancy.
scenes.visual: Column 3 fills: progenitors from stem cells, March 2016; organoids. Infected progenitors glow.
scenes.narration: The laboratory. The virus infected human cortical progenitors most readily, killing some and slowing the rest. A dish cannot show the risk in a pregnancy.

scenes.tts: Predict. The first study used an old Ugandan strain, kept for decades in the lab. What would a skeptic say?
scenes.visual: Label on column 3: strain MR766, isolated in Uganda decades earlier, passaged in the laboratory. Question card.
scenes.narration: Predict. The first study used an old Ugandan strain, kept for decades in the lab. What would a skeptic say?

scenes.tts: That it might not act like the epidemic virus. Later work with epidemic strains agreed.
scenes.visual: Column 3 adds: epidemic strains, organoids and pregnant mice, agree.
scenes.narration: That it might not act like the epidemic virus. Later work with epidemic strains agreed.

scenes.tts: In twenty sixteen, a review against formal criteria concluded that Zika causes microcephaly.
scenes.caption: In 2016, a review against formal criteria concluded that Zika causes microcephaly.
scenes.visual: All three columns light up. Credit: Rasmussen and colleagues, 2016. Conclusion: Zika causes microcephaly and other serious brain defects.
scenes.narration: In 2016, a review against formal criteria concluded that Zika causes microcephaly.

scenes.tts: Two cautions. Most infections in pregnancy do not produce microcephaly. And the virus also damages tissue already built.
scenes.visual: Two caution cards: most infections in pregnancy do not produce microcephaly; destruction as well as too few made.
scenes.narration: Two cautions. Most infections in pregnancy do not produce microcephaly. And the virus also damages tissue already built.

scenes.tts: So a spindle-pole gene, or a virus that finds the same cells, can leave too few neurons.
scenes.visual: Closing card: a spindle-pole gene and a virus, both pointing at the dividing progenitor.
scenes.narration: So a spindle-pole gene, or a virus that finds the same cells, can leave too few neurons.
